extracted.intended_audience: individual authors (independent writers, researchers, scholars, journalists) applying for the NEH Public Scholars grant
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting an application for the National Endowment for the Humanities Public Scholars program to support creation of a well-researched nonfiction book for a broad public audience. Includes eligibility, expected outputs, budget, timelines, application materials, and submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project type — well-researched nonfiction book for the broad public
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Scholars program supports the creation of well-researched nonfiction books in the humanities written for the broad public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program offers grants to individual authors for research, writing, travel, and other activities leading to publication. The expected output for an award is a book intended for a general audience rather than a specialized academic readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility — individuals; no advanced degree required
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers with or without an academic affiliation may apply, and no advanced degree is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH especially encourages applications to this program from independent writers, researchers, scholars, and journalists. The program is open to individuals (not institutions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program purpose / alignment with goals
rubrics_metrics.description: The program is intended to: a) encourage non-academic writers to deepen their engagement with the humanities by strengthening the research underlying their books; and b) encourage academic writers in the humanities to communicate the significance of their research to the broadest possible range of readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should demonstrate how the project furthers these aims — either by deepening humanities research in non-academic writing or by translating academic research for broad public audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special initiative priority — 'A More Perfect Union'
rubrics_metrics.description: A new initiative has been added: “A More Perfect Union”: NEH Special Initiative Advancing Civic Education and Celebrating the Nation’s 250th Anniversary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects aligned with this initiative may receive special encouragement; applicants should indicate alignment with NEH priorities and initiatives where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amount and allowable uses
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants are intended to support research, writing, travel, and other activities leading to publication. Budget requests should be consistent with the monthly cap and used to support the project within the stated period of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected output and period of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Open to individuals. Expected output: Book. Period of performance: Six to twelve months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must plan a project that reasonably produces a book within a six- to twelve-month award period and indicate appropriate project start dates (examples listed: September 1, 2020; September 1, 2021).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application materials and required documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin by reading the full grant guidelines and studying the application. The files are linked below. Download Application Materials: Public Scholar Program Notice of Funding Opportunity (PDF); Public Scholar Program Grants.gov Application Package; Program Resources; Frequently Asked Questions; Sample Application Narratives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should use the provided sample narratives and program resources to model proposals and ensure all required components (narrative, budget, bios, etc.) conform to the Notice of Funding Opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants.gov registration and submission procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Register for a grants.gov account as this is vital to the grants process. If you already have registered, make sure it is up to date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit your application package on Grants.gov. You will receive a confirmation from Grants.gov when you've successfully submitted your application. Follow Grants.gov instructions and the Notice of Funding Opportunity exactly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission confirmations and email verification
rubrics_metrics.description: After you submit your application, Grants.gov will send you up to five e-mail messages confirming receipt of your application. These messages represent different stages in the application acceptance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that you have received all confirmation messages (check spam/junk folders). The applicant is responsible for ensuring they receive these confirmations and for tracking their application's acceptance status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of recommendation management
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH requests letters of reference from your recommenders approximately seven to ten days after the application deadline. You will be notified by e-mail when each of your letters of reference has been received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After receiving the fifth Grants.gov confirmation message (confirming NEH received your application), applicants may check the status of letters by logging in to NEH’s secure area using application and Grants.gov tracking numbers. Applicants are responsible for ensuring letter writers receive solicitations and submit letters; applicants may send reminders (including the upload link) from NEH’s site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical/file-format requirements and tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Download Adobe Reader. Tips for making PDFs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow NEH/Grants.gov technical guidance for preparing electronic application documents (e.g., PDF formatting) so uploaded files are accessible and compliant with submission requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and timeline adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Application available: November 14, 2019. Application due: February 5, 2020. Expected notification date: August 14, 2020. Project start date: September 1, 2020 / September 1, 2021.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must adhere to posted application and project-start deadlines. Timely submission and readiness to begin in the listed project window are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use past funded projects as scope/fit examples
rubrics_metrics.description: List of recently funded Public Scholar Program projects and Sample Application Narratives (examples: Everybody Comes to Rick's; Wild Boar; The Heavens Might Crack; etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should review funded project examples and sample narratives to understand appropriate project scope, level of research, and audience framing for successful applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the Notice of Funding Opportunity and program restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the instructions outlined in the notice of funding opportunity and Grants.gov instructions. You want to ensure you understand all the expectations and restrictions for projects delivered under this grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully conform to stated eligibility, allowable costs, page limits, and other restrictions in the Notice of Funding Opportunity; failure to follow instructions may jeopardize review or funding.
